findings.element: The uppercase micro-label, everywhere it appears: Tasks `.trayName` + `.tag` (tasks.css:149-152, 786-796), Tasks `.lrowLane` (tasks.css:514-520), Notes' FILING UNDER / OTHER WAYS IN / YOUR NOTES / STILL TO DECIDE / HOW IT ARRIVED / LENGTH / LISTENING, Timeline `.b-measureHead` / `.b-todayLabel` / DAYS AWAY / BEHIND YOU / ACROSS / DOWN (timeline.css --track-label)
findings.problem: One typographic role - the small-caps eyebrow that names a region - is set six ways in one application. Swept every uppercase string in all ten states at 1440: Notes Geist SANS 11/600 +0.075em (13 sites) and 12/600 +0.075em (1); Tasks board Geist MONO 11/400 +0.10em (40); Tasks list Geist SANS 11/600 +0.075em; Timeline Geist MONO 11/400 +0.16em (14) and 12/400 +0.20em (3). Two families, two weights, four tracks. Three consequences, all verified by driving. (1) Weight carries different information in different rooms: in Notes the eyebrow is 600, the same weight as its titles, so weight does not separate label from title; in Tasks and Timeline it is 400 and it does. (2) Tasks sets the role twice inside itself - drag the window from 1201 to 1199, the recorded board floor, and TO DO / IN PROGRESS / REVIEW / WAITING / DONE change typeface, weight and ink density; and `.lrowLane` reaches for `--tr-cap`, which tasks.css:75-85 declares as the step for "a monogram, which is the one string in this product that is a letterform rather than a word", and spends it on words. (3) The two voices meet on one line: in every list row at 390 and at 1199, cropped at 4x, "TO DO" sits at the left in Geist sans 600 +0.075em and "VENUE" at the right in Geist Mono 400 +0.10em - same 11px, same uppercase, same ink at 0.62 - 250px apart on one baseline. Neither gate can see this, because the audit groups letterfit by product + family + size, so two families at one size never land in the same group. This is not the ratified-tracking exclusion: three ratified tracking curves do not license two families and two weights for one role.
findings.fix: Hoist the role to one declaration in shell.css beside the keycap that was hoisted the same way in round 6, and leave the products only their ink and their placement. Add to shell.css: `--t-label: 11px; --tr-label: 0.16em;` on `:root`, and `.capLabel { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: var(--t-label); font-weight: 400; line-height: 14px; letter-spacing: var(--tr-label); text-transform: uppercase; }`. Then delete the family / size / weight / letter-spacing declarations from `[data-app="tasks"] .trayName` (tasks.css:149-152), `[data-app="tasks"] .tag`, `[data-app="tasks"] .lrowLane` (tasks.css:514-520, keeping only its display, gap, colour and ellipsis), Notes' 11px `--tr-cap` label rules and the 12px `.darkTag`, and Timeline's `--track-label` rules, adding `capLabel` to those elements' class lists. Keep exactly two declared exceptions and no more: `--tr-cap: 0.075em` reverts to what its own comment says it is - the monogram step, used only by `.railAvatar` / `.dockAvatar`; and Timeline's `--track-labelWide: 0.20em` stays for the ceremonial top line its token comment already restricts it to. The value 0.16em is arguable, 0.10em would also do; the count of one is not. Validated by driving the substitution (Geist Mono / 400 / +0.16em applied to every uppercase micro-label) at 390, 768, 1280, 1440 and 1920 on notebook, board, dense, review and voice: zero labels wrapped to a new line, zero clipped, zero new sideways scroll; the largest single growth is 24.4px on STILL TO DECIDE, which sits alone on a rule with room, and the largest inside Tasks is 7.3px.

findings.problem: On the across axis the row of dates under the measure breaks its own baseline, and only on one side. Above the axis `.b-copy` is anchored by `bottom:`, so `.b-date` tops sit at 623 for every moment whether the title ran one line or two - one clean row. Below the axis `.b-copy` is anchored by `top:`, so the date floats: 752 for the one-line titles ("Send the invitations", "Venue walk-through") and 774 for the two-line one ("Choose the evening music"). A 22px step, identical at 1024, 1280, 1440 and 1920, in a row of dates that is the scale of the instrument the whole direction is built on. Above the axis a wrapping title costs nothing; below it, one wrapped title drops its date a full line and reads as a fallen item.
findings.fix: Give the title one height on both sides so `.b-copy` is one box either way, and hug the axis-facing edge so no words move. In src/across.css, after the `.b-title` rule at line 278, add: `[data-app="timeline"] .b-measure[data-across="true"] .b-title { min-height: calc(2 * var(--lead-body) * var(--size-body)); display: flex; }` then `[data-app="timeline"] .b-measure[data-across="true"] .b-item[data-side="above"] .b-title { align-items: flex-end; }` and `[data-app="timeline"] .b-measure[data-across="true"] .b-item[data-side="below"] .b-title { align-items: flex-start; }`. Above the axis nothing moves (the block is bottom-anchored and grows upward into space that is already empty); below it every date lands on the row the wrapped one already occupies. `placeAcross` measures `--step` and `--away-h` from the labels that actually rendered, so the ranks re-space themselves; the cost is that the below half of the track reserves one more line of body leading.

findings.element: `[data-app="tasks"] .lrows` grid under the 720 fold, tasks.css:573-580, with `.lrow .when[data-t="none"] { visibility: hidden }` at tasks.css:563
findings.problem: On a phone the list gives a person's own words 14 to 22 characters a line. The fold sets `grid-template-columns: 34px minmax(0,1fr) 74px`; `.lrowSay` takes column 2 row 1 and `.when` takes column 3 row 1, so 74px of row 1 is reserved for the date chip on every row - including the rows that have no date, where the chip is only `visibility: hidden` and still holds its cell. Driven and measured on tasks.board: `.lrowSay` is 116px at 320 (about 14 characters at 13px), 186px at 390 (about 22, inside a 322px row) and 226px at 430 (about 27). Five of thirteen rows on the board and seventeen of thirty-two in dense carry no day at all and pay the 74px anyway. Tasks already argued this exact problem out on the desk and solved it with a float - tasks.css:911-918, "the date chip was stealing width from all three lines instead of one" - and the phone re-introduces it as a grid reserve. Twenty-two characters is below any measure floor for continuous prose; the fixture's notes run three and four lines at 390 and seven lines at 320 because of it.
findings.fix: Release the day's column on the rows that have no day. In tasks.css, inside the existing `@media (max-width: 720px)` block at line 573, add: `[data-app="tasks"] .lrow:not(:has(.when:not([data-t="none"]))) .lrowSay { grid-column: 2 / -1; }`. Driven at 320, 390 and 430 on board, dense and compact: `.lrowSay` goes 116 to 198px at 320, 186 to 268px at 390, 226 to 308px at 430; thirteen fewer wrapped lines at 320, five at 390, seven in dense at 390; no overlap with `.lrowMeta` (which is row 2) and no sideways scroll at any width. That is the CSS-only half. The other half - the rows that DO carry a chip, whose lines 2, 3 and 4 are still capped at 186px by a chip that only occupies line 1 - needs the chip moved inside `.lrowSay` as a float, exactly as `.cardTitleRow` carries it on the desk; that is a DOM change and should be costed separately.

findings.element: Notes' tracking curve, notes.css:106-108, against Notes' type ramp, notes.css:89-90
findings.problem: The curve is indexed at 11, 12, 14, 16, 18, 21, 27, 34. The ramp it serves is 11, 12, 13, 15, 17, 20, 27, 34. Four of the eight ramp sizes - 13, 15, 17 and 20 - have no step of their own, so every rule at those sizes borrows a neighbour by hand, and the file borrows different neighbours for the same size: `--t-17` takes `--tr-18` (-0.021em) in `.topField`, `.pick`, `.sent` and `.idxDay`, `--tr-16` (-0.016em) in `.peelSent`, and `--tr-21` (-0.026em) elsewhere; `--t-15` takes both `--tr-16` and `--tr-14`; `--t-13` takes both `--tr-14` and `--tr-12`. The token block above them says "One tracking curve, by size, declared once. Every letter-spacing in this file is a token from it." The visible instance is on the protected object: drive lift, select, peel, send, and the receipt sets the picked sentence "Ceremony 2pm in the orchard, drinks on the" at 17px/600 and -0.016em directly under the same sentence on the desk at 17px/400 and -0.021em - the heavier setting given the looser fit, which is backwards.
findings.fix: Re-index the curve onto the ramp it serves. In notes.css:106-108 replace the eight steps with `--tr-34: -0.034em; --tr-27: -0.030em; --tr-20: -0.026em; --tr-17: -0.020em; --tr-15: -0.016em; --tr-13: -0.010em; --tr-12: -0.006em; --tr-11: 0em;` - the same curve, sampled at the sizes that exist - then replace every borrowed reference with the step for the size the rule declares (`--t-17` rules take `--tr-17`, `--t-15` take `--tr-15`, `--t-13` take `--tr-13`, `--t-20` takes `--tr-20`). Keep `--tr-cap: 0.075em` and `--tr-key: 0.04em` where they are: they are ROLE steps, not size steps, and they are the two the size index must not swallow. After this every size in Notes has exactly one letterfit and the comment above the block is true.

findings.element: The Tasks card panel `.taskPanel` - `.tpLane`, its three `h3` micro-labels, five `dt` and five `dd`, `.tpSrc` - and `[data-app="tasks"] .pacePct` (tasks.css:325-328)
findings.problem: The type system is declared exactly as far as the gate's ten fixture states reach, and no further. Swept every visible text element in all ten states for a browser-chosen line-height: zero hits, in any state, at any width - the leading ladder holds completely. Then drove one surface the gate cannot reach, the panel a person lands on when they press a card, and found fourteen elements at `line-height: normal` and one at `letter-spacing: normal`. They land on the ladder today only because Geist's own metrics happen to give 1.273 at 11px (14px, a declared step) and 1.308 at 13px (17px, another declared step); a fallback face while Geist loads, or any change to its metrics, moves that surface off the ladder and nothing will catch it. The one undeclared letterfit is `.tpSrc`, "Came from a note in Notes" - the seam's own return door, and the only string in the panel with no letterfit while every sibling at 13px carries -0.010em. Separately, and the only one of its kind in the whole suite: `.pacePct` ("38%") declares family, size, weight, colour and tabular figures but no letter-spacing, so it inherits -0.13px from `.headFacts` - a letterfit computed for 13px SANS, landing on an 11px MONO figure as -0.0118em, while the other mono figure in the same header band, `.trayCount`, sits at +0.10em. Sweeping every element in all ten states for a letterfit inherited across a size or family change returns exactly one hit, and it is this one.
findings.fix: Three declarations. (1) In tasks.css, give the panel its leading from the ladder: `[data-app="tasks"] .taskPanel .tpLane, [data-app="tasks"] .taskPanel h3 { line-height: 14px; }` and `[data-app="tasks"] .taskPanel dt, [data-app="tasks"] .taskPanel dd, [data-app="tasks"] .taskPanel .tpNone { line-height: 17px; }` - the values it renders today, now written down. (2) `[data-app="tasks"] .tpSrc { letter-spacing: var(--tr-13); }`, matching every other 13px string in the panel. (3) Add a mono step to Tasks' curve beside the cap step it already carries - `--tr-data: 0.04em;`, the value Notes declares as `--tr-key` and Timeline as `--track-data` - and add `letter-spacing: var(--tr-data);` to `[data-app="tasks"] .pacePct` at tasks.css:326. Then add one assertion to interaction-check.mjs that opens a card and fails any element inside `.taskPanel` whose computed `line-height` or `letter-spacing` is `normal`, so the next surface reachable only by driving is not declared by the browser either.

biggestWin: The measure and the trim. Every surface that carries a person's own writing is held to 31em and renders at 59 to 64 characters a line - driven and counted in the compose field, the reading body and the peel - which is textbook and rare; and across ten states at five widths I could not produce a single mid-word clip, a single mixed letterfit inside one line of type, or a single counter that ticks in proportional figures, including the live character counter. Underneath that, the tracking curve composes a polarity branch correctly - the dock's reversed "Add task" computes -0.002em because it is --tr-13 plus --tr-rev, and "1 overdue" computes +0.002em because it is --tr-12 plus --tr-rev - which is a system doing arithmetic rather than a designer typing numbers, and it is more type system than most shipped products carry.
